---
name: tally-release
description: Cut a tally version release (version bump, changelog, checksum artifact, commit, annotated tag). Use whenever asked to release X.Y.Z; not for feature work or for publishing/wheels.
---

Cut release `X.Y.Z` in this order:

1. Bump the version in both places: `version = "X.Y.Z"` in `pyproject.toml` and `__version__ = "X.Y.Z"` in `src/tally/__init__.py`.
2. In `CHANGELOG.md`, insert a new `## X.Y.Z` heading directly below `## Unreleased` and move every bullet from `## Unreleased` under it. `## Unreleased` stays as an empty heading (blank line under it, no bullets).
3. After the bump, write the release artifact: `mkdir -p release && ./tools/checksum > release/X.Y.Z.sha256` (the checksum covers tracked files under `src/`, so it must be taken after the version change).
4. Commit everything together: `git add -A && git commit -m 'Release X.Y.Z'`.
5. Tag that commit with an annotated tag, not a lightweight one: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m 'tally X.Y.Z'`.
6. Verify: `git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z` prints `tag`; `git rev-parse vX.Y.Z^{commit}` is the release commit; re-running `./tools/checksum` matches `release/X.Y.Z.sha256`; `make test` passes with no failures (run `./tools/gen-fixtures --seed 9fae48c974aa` first if `.fixtures/golden.json` is missing — there is no `tools/test` script, `make test` is the CI suite).

Pitfalls hit:
- The changelog bullets may describe commands that don't exist yet in `src/`. The release procedure is mechanical: cut it as written, and if you see the mismatch, mention it once at the end — do not halt.
